title: Case Escalation Email Alert to Account Owner

requirement.summary: When a Case linked to an Account is escalated (Case.IsEscalated becomes true), automatically email the Account Owner so they are aware their customer is unhappy; the email includes the Case Number and Subject. Delivered as a single after-save record-triggered Flow on Case, design-only (no org access), scale: feature due to two named objects (Case, Account).

clarifications.question: Which field represents "escalated" in this org (the standard Case.IsEscalated checkbox, a custom field, or a Status value), and if a Case is escalated, un-escalated, and later re-escalated, should each new escalation send a fresh email or only the very first one ever?
clarifications.why: Decides the flow's trigger field and doesRequireRecordChangedToMeetCriteria; the wrong field misses real escalations, and the wrong transition-vs-repeat answer either sends nothing on a repeat escalation or spams the owner on every unrelated edit.
clarifications.proposed_default: Standard Case.IsEscalated checkbox. Every new transition into true (including a repeat escalation after being un-escalated) sends a fresh email, since each represents a new unhappy-customer event; edits that leave IsEscalated unchanged never re-fire it.
clarifications.answer_shape: The field API name, plus a yes/no on whether repeat escalations re-notify.
clarifications.answer: Yes, whatever our standard Escalated flag/checkbox is on the Case — we don't use a separate custom field for that. And yes please: if a case gets un-escalated and then escalated again later, send the email again each time. We'd rather get a duplicate heads-up than miss one.

clarifications.question: Who should the notification email appear to come from, and does anyone need to monitor replies to that address?
clarifications.why: Sender identity is an org-wide email address that must exist and be verified in the target org before the flow can send from it.
clarifications.proposed_default: Send from the org's default Organization-Wide Email Address (fall back to the flow's running-user context if none is configured). No reply monitoring is needed — the Account Owner is expected to open the Case in Salesforce rather than reply by email.
clarifications.answer_shape: A named Organization-Wide Email Address (or explicit decision not to use one) and whether replies need a monitored mailbox.
clarifications.answer: Just send it from whatever our normal Salesforce notification address is — I don't need to pick a specific inbox. Nobody needs to reply to the email; the account owner should just go look at the case in Salesforce.

clarifications.question: What should happen if the Case has no related Account, or the Account has no Owner (or the owner is a Queue rather than a person)? Who, if anyone, should be notified instead?
clarifications.why: "Make it automatic" hides the exception path; without a decision, a null Account or Owner either silently drops the alert or fails invisibly inside the flow's own error email.
clarifications.proposed_default: If the Case has no related Account, skip the email and log the skip. If the Account Owner is a Queue rather than a User, send to the queue's email address if one exists; otherwise fall back to notifying the Support Manager / Case-escalation admin distribution list. No customer-facing failure either way.
clarifications.answer_shape: A named decision and fallback recipient for each of the two null/edge cases.
clarifications.answer: If a case somehow isn't linked to an account, don't worry about it — that's an edge case, skip it. If the account is owned by a queue/team instead of a real person, send it to whoever manages that team as a backup — our support manager is a fine default for now.

clarifications.question: If the Get-Account-Owner or Send-Email step fails (bad address, deleted user, etc.), who should find out, and how?
clarifications.why: Without a fault path the interview stops and the error is invisible outside the flow's own error email, which nobody but the running user ever sees.
clarifications.proposed_default: The fault path writes an entry using the repo's standard flow-fault logging pattern (Application_Log__c, per templates/flow/FaultPath_Template.md) and emails the Salesforce admin distribution list. No customer-facing impact.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of the fault-logging target and who is on the admin distribution list.
clarifications.answer: If it breaks, just let whoever manages Salesforce for us know so they can fix it — however that's normally handled is fine, I don't need a separate process for this.

clarifications.question: Does this change touch only fields on the Case being saved, or does it also need to read the related Account/Owner and send email?
clarifications.why: Same-record-only work fits a before-save flow; anything that sends email or reads a related object forces after-save.
clarifications.proposed_default: After-save — the flow reads the related Account's Owner and sends email, neither of which a before-save flow can do (confirmed by standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md Q2/Q4/Q5).
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation of RecordAfterSave as the trigger type.
clarifications.answer: After-save — the flow reads the related Account's Owner and sends email, neither of which a before-save flow can do (confirmed by standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md Q2/Q4/Q5).

clarifications.question: What else already runs on Case in the after-save context, and does this new flow need to run before or after any of it?
clarifications.why: Two flows in one save context with no declared order is undefined sequencing.
clarifications.proposed_default: No other after-save automation is known to depend on ordering relative to this notification; run at the default triggerOrder. This flow never writes back to the Case, so it cannot conflict with another flow's field ownership.

clarifications.question: Does anything downstream update this Case again as a result of this flow, creating a recursion risk?
clarifications.why: An after-save flow that re-saves its own object re-enters the save procedure and can behave differently on the second pass.
clarifications.proposed_default: No — this flow only sends an email and never performs DML on the Case or Account, so there is no recursion risk and no recursion guard is needed.

clarifications.question: Should the email send immediately when the Case is escalated, or can/should it be delayed (e.g., batched, or gated to business hours)?
clarifications.why: A delayed notification needs a FlowScheduledPath; an immediate one does not.
clarifications.proposed_default: Immediate — send synchronously in the same after-save transaction. Do not gate on business hours; an unhappy customer alert loses its value if it waits for morning.
clarifications.answer_shape: Immediate vs. a named delay/business-hours gate.
clarifications.answer: Immediate — send synchronously in the same after-save transaction. Do not gate on business hours; an unhappy customer alert loses its value if it waits for morning.

clarifications.question: When a Case of this kind is deleted, does anything about this notification need to be preserved or cleaned up?
clarifications.why: RecordBeforeDelete is the only delete context that exists for record-triggered flows, and there is no after-delete equivalent.
clarifications.proposed_default: Not applicable — this flow only reacts to Case updates (escalation), not deletes; no delete-context flow is needed.
clarifications.answer_shape: Confirmation no delete-context handling is required.
clarifications.answer: Not applicable — this flow only reacts to Case updates (escalation), not deletes; no delete-context flow is needed.

clarifications.question: Roughly how many Cases get escalated per day (steady state and worst case), to confirm this stays well under the org's mass-email and Flow governor limits?

in: Send an automated email to the Account Owner whenever a Case on that Account is escalated (Case.IsEscalated transitions to true), including the Case Number and Subject in the email (Q1, requirement statement).
Fire on every new transition into escalated, including a repeat escalation after a Case was previously un-escalated, not only the first-ever escalation (Q1).

Handle the no-related-Account and no-person-Owner (Queue-owned Account) edge cases explicitly rather than letting them fail silently: skip-and-log for no Account, fall back to the Support Manager distribution list when the owner is a Queue (Q3).
A fault path that logs any send failure and notifies the Salesforce admin distribution list (Q4).
out: Building or modifying native Salesforce Escalation Rules (the mechanism that sets IsEscalated in the first place) — the requirement only asks to react to an escalation that already happens; confirmed no engine change is requested and the native engine's own notify actions cannot target a dynamically-resolved Account Owner (see D1 rationale).
Any change to Case routing/assignment on creation — out of scope; not mentioned in the requirement and no clarification implied it.
In-app bell / SMS / Slack notification channels — the requirement asks specifically for email (Q11 default); other channels are a separate ask.
Reporting or a dashboard on escalation notifications sent — explicitly descoped at Q19; the email itself is the entire deliverable.
Any sharing, field-level-security, or licence change — explicitly descoped at Q15/Q18; the flow runs in automation context and needs no new user-facing visibility.

fit_gap.requirement: Email the Account Owner (with Case Number and Subject) whenever a Case on that Account is escalated
fit_gap.note: A single after-save record-triggered Flow on Case, reading the related Account's Owner and sending email via the Send Email action, satisfies the requirement natively — no Apex, no managed package. Tiered per skills/admin/fit-gap-analysis-against-org: the moment a Flow is in the delivery path the row is Low-Code, regardless of how simple the automation reads.

decisions.decision: Build the notification as a Flow rather than relying on the native Escalation Rules engine's own notify actions, and rather than Apex.
decisions.rationale: Q1 (record change) -> Q2 ('No' branch, since sending email and reading a related object crosses objects) -> Q4 asks whether the logic needs to cross objects (DML on related records, send email, create tasks); the answer is yes, which routes to Q5. Escalation Rules' own escalationAction (notifyTo/notifyEmail/notifyCaseOwner) targets a fixed user, role, or the case owner — read in skills/admin/escalation-rules/SKILL.md's Core Concepts table — and cannot dynamically resolve 'the Owner of the Case's related Account', so the native engine cannot satisfy this requirement regardless of whether escalation itself is already configured natively or manually. Apex is not warranted: none of automation-selection.md Q3's Apex triggers (governor-limit risk, retry/backoff callouts, complex rollback, recursive DML, coverage-gated deploy, custom exception types) apply to a single-record, single-email send.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q4. Does the logic need to cross objects (DML on related records, send email, create tasks)?
    ├── No   → After-save record-triggered Flow
    └── Yes  → Q5
decisions.consequences: The notification lives in Flow Builder, editable by an admin without a deploy for entry-criteria tweaks, but is a second place (besides any existing Escalation Rule) that reacts to IsEscalated — documented in the step note so a future admin does not assume Escalation Rules already cover this.

decisions.decision: Use an After-Save record-triggered Flow on Case (Update only), firing inline (not on a Scheduled Path), rather than Before-Save.
decisions.rationale: flow-pattern-selector.md Q1 (record UPDATE) -> Q2 ('No', since the flow reads the related Account and sends email, not only same-record fields) -> Q4 (Yes, the action — sending email — must happen after the triggering DML commits) -> Q5 (No, the action is not time-relative to the record; the whole point of an escalation alert is that it fires now). Before-Save is structurally unable to send email or read a related record for anything beyond a lazy-loaded field lookup (skills/flow/record-triggered-flow-patterns Core Concepts, 'What before-save CANNOT do').
decisions.branch_quote:
Q5. Does the action need to happen at a specific time RELATIVE to the record
    (e.g. "30 days after Close Date", "1 hour before SLA breach")?
    ├── Yes  → After-Save record-triggered flow with Scheduled Path (entry criteria gates the schedule)
    └── No   → After-Save record-triggered flow, firing inline
decisions.consequences: The email sends synchronously in the triggering transaction; a Send Email failure must be caught by a fault path (Q4) rather than retried later, since there is no scheduled path to fall back to.

milestones.title: Email the Account Owner when a Case is escalated
milestones.goal: Given a Case linked to an Account, when the Case transitions to IsEscalated = true (including a repeat escalation after being un-escalated), then an email is sent to the Account's Owner containing the Case Number and Subject; given the Case has no related Account, then no email is sent and the skip is logged; given the Account Owner is a Queue with no email, then the email is sent to the Support Manager distribution list instead; given the flow's Get-Owner or Send-Email step fails, then a fault-path log entry is written and the Salesforce admin distribution list is notified, with no unhandled fault.

acceptance_tests.description: Given a Case linked to an Account owned by a real user, when an admin checks the Case's Escalated checkbox and saves, then the Account Owner receives an email within the same interaction containing the Case Number and Subject; when the same Case is un-escalated and re-escalated, a second email arrives; when a Case with no Account is escalated, no email is sent and a log entry records the skip; when a Case whose Account is owned by a Queue with no email is escalated, the Support Manager distribution list receives the email instead.
acceptance_tests.expected: ticked at the M1 milestone gate

steps.title: After-save record-triggered Flow on Case: email Account Owner when escalated

inputs.entry_criteria: IsEscalated changes to true (doesRequireRecordChangedToMeetCriteria: true; filter IsEscalated EqualTo true)
inputs.repeat_fire: Every new transition into IsEscalated=true re-fires the flow, including a repeat escalation after being un-escalated (Q1 answer)
inputs.related_lookup: Get the Case's Account, then look up the Account's OwnerId against the User object; a Get Records on User returning no row means the owner is a Group/Queue rather than a person

send_email.mechanism: Flow Send Email action (emailSimple) with inline text (Q11 answer)
send_email.to: Account.Owner's email (Get_Owner_User.Email) when the Owner is a User; a Custom Label fallback address (Support-Manager distribution list) when no matching User record is found (Q3 answer)
send_email.subject: Case {!$Record.CaseNumber} escalated: {!$Record.Subject}
body_merge_fields: direct link to the Case record
send_email.no_account_behavior: If Case.AccountId is blank, skip the Send Email and write an INFO Application_Log__c entry instead (Q3 answer)

inputs.fault_path: On every Get-Records and Send-Email element, a faultConnector routes to a shared Capture_Fault -> Create_Application_Log_Error (ERROR) -> Notify_Admin_On_Fault (emailSimple to the admin Custom Label) chain per templates/flow/FaultPath_Template.md, with the log-write and admin-notify steps backstopping each other's own faultConnector so no DML/action element in the flow is left without one (Q4 answer)
inputs.sender_identity: Org default Organization-Wide Email Address, or the flow's running-user context if none is configured; no reply monitoring required (Q2 answer)
inputs.emailSimple_action_shape: The Flow 'Send Email' core action is actionName/actionType `emailSimple`, with inputParameters `emailAddresses`, `emailSubject`, and `emailBodyRichText` (or `emailBody` for plain text) -- the exact deployable shape, including a real after-save-Case-plus-fault-path worked example, is in skills/admin/flow-for-admins/references/metadata-examples.md Example 2, not in either of the other two cited skills. Neither flow/record-triggered-flow-patterns (which documents trigger/entry-criteria/fault-connector shape but not action-specific inputParameters) nor admin/email-templates-and-alerts (which documents classic EmailTemplate/EmailAlert metadata, explicitly not Flow's own Send Email action) supplies these parameter names, so admin/flow-for-admins was added to skills[] after the plan-verifier's grounding lens caught the gap on the first verification pass.
inputs.email_templates_checker_note: admin/email-templates-and-alerts/scripts/check_email_templates.py only audits classic EmailTemplate/.email-meta.xml artefacts (confirmed: running it against a fixture holding only a .flow-meta.xml file returns ERROR 'no email template artefact found', exit 1). This step deliberately produces no such artefact -- the email content lives inline inside the Flow's emailSimple action, per decision D1/Q11 -- so that checker can never be satisfied by this step's correct output and was removed from acceptance_tests[] by amend-step after the plan-verifier's testability lens caught it on the first verification pass. The skill itself remains cited in skills[] for its prose guidance (sender identity, merge-context scoping); only its checker was inapplicable.
